children: The Government Expenditure and Projects Efficiency Authority (EXPRO) has announced the activation of flynas under the unified framework agreement for government travel services, in cooperation with the Ministry of Finance and the National Centre for Government Resource Systems.

The move increases the number of participating airlines to four, alongside Saudia, flyadeal and Riyadh Air, strengthening competition and expanding travel options for government employees and beneficiaries of government travel services.

The addition of flynas is expected to increase seat capacity, expand destination coverage and flight schedules, and provide greater booking flexibility and a wider range of service packages to meet the needs of public-sector travellers.

The activation will also expand travel options available through the Etimad platform, providing an integrated digital process covering travel order creation, flight booking and electronic ticket issuance.
EXPRO said the initiative will help improve operational efficiency while enhancing the customer experience.
The unified procurement framework is one of EXPRO’s contracting mechanisms for government entities under the Government Tenders and Procurement Law.

It enables the authority to negotiate unified agreements with service providers to achieve better value for public funds, reduce procurement time, standardize prices and service specifications, and improve service quality.

EXPRO said flynas’ activation forms part of its efforts to diversify suppliers and expand the number of participating carriers, supporting greater flexibility and efficiency in government travel services while meeting the evolving needs of government entities and beneficiaries.

title: ZAWYA: EXPRO adds flynas to government travel agreement
